title: Bridging Mesoscopic and Microscopic Scales in Multiple Sclerosis: MRI and Histology Quantification
author: Gkotsoulias, Schönenberger, et al.
materials: blocks from brains of adult multiple sclerosis patients

steps.title: Retrieve brain block from PFA
steps.instruction: Take the brain block of interest, stored at room temperature (≈23 °C) and submerged in 4 % paraformaldehyde (PFA) solution.

steps.title: Dry specimen gently
steps.instruction: Remove the specimen from the PFA solution and gently pat dry with a paper towel.

steps.title: Immerse specimen in Fomblin
steps.instruction: Place the specimen in perfluoropolyether (Fomblin; Solvay Solexis, Bollate, Italy) inside a cylindrical glass container (25 mm diameter, 100 mm length) so it fits the MRI receiver coil.

steps.title: Add PMMA levitation cylinder
steps.instruction: Put a Polymethyl‑Methacrylate (PMMA) cylinder (22 mm diameter, 15 mm height) onto the bottom of the tube to lift the sample away from strong susceptibility gradients.

steps.title: Stabilize with PMMA supports
steps.instruction: Insert non‑magnetic PMMA spheres (6.4 mm diameter) and PMMA plates (thickness 2 mm and 3 mm; width 15 mm; height 3.5 cm and 4 cm) longitudinally to keep the specimen centered in the tube.

steps.title: Remove air bubbles and plug cylinder
steps.instruction: Gently move the sample to expel any cavitated air bubbles from the field of view, then insert the 22 mm × 15 mm PMMA cylinder plugs into the tube.

steps.title: Load tube into RF coil
steps.instruction: Place the tube containing the perfluoropolyether‑immersed, stabilized specimen into the 25 mm bird‑cage receiver RF coil and mount the coil assembly into the Bruker Avance Neo 400 WB spectrometer.

steps.title: Perform survey scan for bubbles
steps.instruction: Run a quick survey MRI scan to verify that no air‑tissue interface bubbles are present before the full‑scan session.

steps.title: Observe safety precautions
steps.instruction: Handle PFA in a certified fume hood with lab coat, chemical‑resistant gloves, and safety goggles; treat perfluoropolyether with gloves; follow institutional waste‑disposal rules for both chemicals.
